island: Minjerribah / North Stradbroke Island, Quandamooka Country, Queensland, Australia
honesty: Every entry here is a real trading business, club, service or public agency unless its status field says otherwise.
Nothing in this file was invented. Where a name could not be confirmed as still trading it carries confidence low and a note.
Coordinates marked coords_source 'luke-repo-workbook' come from Luke's own place workbook and are entrance-approximate, not survey grade.
All employs figures and all peak_multiplier_estimate figures are modelling estimates for the simulation, not measured headcounts or measured trade data.
Hours with basis 'estimate' are a plausible island pattern for the simulation to run on, not published trading hours. Do not display them to a player as fact.

field_guide.id: stable slug, safe to use as a key
field_guide.name: current trading name
field_guide.also_known_as: former or alternate trading names locals still use
field_guide.township: Dunwich (Goompi) | Point Lookout (Mulumba) | Amity Point (Pulan) | One Mile | Island-wide | Mainland terminal
field_guide.address: street address as published, null if not confirmed
field_guide.lat / lon: WGS84 decimal degrees, null if not confirmed
field_guide.typical_hours: weekly pattern. Values: 'HH:MM-HH:MM', 'closed', 'unverified', or '24h'. basis says whether published or estimated
field_guide.seasonality: how the long weekend and school holiday surge changes this place. peak_multiplier_estimate is a modelling multiplier on normal-week demand
field_guide.employs: rough headcount range in normal trade, basis always 'estimate' unless stated
field_guide.role_in_sim: one line on what this does in a simulation of island life
field_guide.note: anything a local would correct us on

businesses.name: Stradbroke Island Beach Hotel
businesses.address: 158 East Coast Road, Point Lookout QLD 4183

seasonality.pattern: The single biggest crowd sink on the island. Long weekends, New Year and school holidays fill the bistro, the bar and the 28 rooms at once, and the pressure lands on staff housing and on the last bus home.

businesses.role_in_sim: Anchor venue for evening crowd, live music nights and visitor accommodation load; drives late-night transport demand.
businesses.note: Operated within the Moreton Hospitality group. Bistro and bar are branded separately (Manta Ray Bistro, Waves Bar); locals just say the pub.

businesses.name: Pandanus Palms Resort

seasonality.pattern: Self-contained villas, so it fills with families on multi-night stays rather than day trippers. Books out well ahead for Christmas and Easter and empties midweek out of season.

businesses.role_in_sim: Hillside villa accommodation; a source of multi-night family visitors and of cleaning and linen work for residents.
businesses.note: Street address not confirmed from a primary source, so lat/lon left null rather than guessed.

businesses.name: Whalewatch Ocean Beach Resort

seasonality.pattern: Sits on the dunes above Main Beach, so whale season from June to November is a real selling season here, not just a summer business.

businesses.role_in_sim: Ocean-facing apartments; ties visitor numbers to the whale migration window rather than to summer alone.
businesses.note: Address not confirmed from a primary source.

businesses.name: Anchorage on Straddie

seasonality.pattern: Holiday apartments near Home Beach and Cylinder Beach; peaks with the family beach season and long weekends.

businesses.role_in_sim: Apartment accommodation with a small retail arcade at ground level; a visitor cluster on the Dickson Way side.
businesses.source: repo: C:/Users/sbt41/githublocal/quandamooka-country-events-engine/assets/place-data-extra.js (Noreen's Seaside Shop listed at Shop 1, Anchorage on Straddie, 112 Dickson Way)
businesses.note: Coordinates are for the building, taken from the shop tenancy record rather than from the resort's own listing.

businesses.name: Allure Stradbroke Resort

seasonality.pattern: Larger resort stock within walking distance of Cylinder Beach; carries a share of the peak-season overflow that campgrounds cannot take.

businesses.role_in_sim: Resort accommodation with an on-site food outlet (Straddie Eats); a concentrated visitor node near Cylinder Beach.
businesses.source: repo: C:/Users/sbt41/githublocal/stradbroke-grants-lab/data/entities.json (I AM Straddie 2025 trail listing) plus https://www.accommodationstradbroke.com.au/play/stradbroke-island-restaurants/
businesses.note: Confirmed as a Point Lookout resort in two listings; exact street address not confirmed.

businesses.name: Manta Lodge & Scuba Centre

seasonality.pattern: Dive demand follows water clarity and the manta season at Manta Bommie more than it follows school holidays. Backpacker beds fill in summer; dive trips run whenever the swell allows.

businesses.role_in_sim: The island's dive operation and its budget bed stock; couples weather and sea state directly to visitor activity and income.
businesses.note: Opened 1992. The YHA branding appears in older listings; current material trades as Manta Lodge & Scuba Centre, so treat 'YHA' as a former name.

businesses.name: The Islander Holiday Resort

seasonality.pattern: Standard Point Lookout holiday letting pattern: full over summer and Easter, quiet midweek in winter.

businesses.role_in_sim: Additional Point Lookout accommodation stock.
businesses.note: Website exists but current trading status was not independently confirmed. Verify with a local before showing this one to a player.

businesses.name: Minjerribah Camping

seasonality.pattern: The hardest peak on the island. Camping and 4WD beach permits all run through this one office, so every holiday arrival wave hits it at once, and Flinders and Main Beach camping is the first thing to close in fire or flood weather.

businesses.role_in_sim: Single control point for campground occupancy and beach vehicle permits; the lever a planner pulls to change visitor load without touching the ferry.
businesses.note: Owned outright by QYAC since November 2017. Runs the beachfront campgrounds (Adder Rock, Cylinder Beach, Home Beach, Amity Point, Bradbury's Beach, Adams Beach, Flinders Beach, Main Beach) plus cabins.

businesses.name: Ray White North Stradbroke Island

seasonality.pattern: Check-in and check-out days set the rhythm: Friday and Saturday turnovers create a cleaning and linen surge across the whole township on the same morning.

businesses.role_in_sim: Largest holiday letting book on the island; converts private houses into visitor beds and generates the Saturday changeover work wave.

businesses.name: Discover Stradbroke Real Estate
businesses.address: Suite 3, 23 Mooloomba Road, Point Lookout QLD 4183

seasonality.pattern: Same changeover pattern as the other agencies, with a smaller book. Sales enquiry rises after a good holiday season.

businesses.role_in_sim: Second holiday letting agency; a second source of changeover work and of the visitor information that reaches guests.

businesses.name: Straddie Sales & Rentals

seasonality.pattern: Amity's letting stock is smaller and quieter than Point Lookout's, and skews to fishing families and repeat visitors rather than first-timers.

businesses.role_in_sim: The Amity Point letting agency; keeps the western township's visitor economy separate from Point Lookout's.

businesses.name: Dolphin Property Sales
businesses.address: Shop 1, 2 Meegera Place, Point Lookout QLD 4183

seasonality.pattern: Lets across all three townships, so its changeover load is spread rather than concentrated at Point Lookout.

businesses.role_in_sim: Third letting agency, with stock at Point Lookout, Amity Point and Dunwich.

businesses.name: Fishes at the Point

seasonality.pattern: Opposite the North Gorge walk, so it catches walkers all year and is one of the few places open every day. Queues out the door on holiday weekends; steady locals trade the rest of the year.

businesses.role_in_sim: All-day food anchor at the gorge end of the village; the default meal stop for a walker who did not plan lunch.
businesses.note: Listing states open every day of the year, 8am to 9pm.

businesses.name: The Blue Room

seasonality.pattern: Breakfast and lunch only, so it takes the morning wave rather than the evening one. Small room, so peak season shows up as a wait rather than as more covers.

businesses.role_in_sim: Small ocean-view breakfast and lunch cafe; a capacity-limited venue that generates visible queues under load.
businesses.note: Address conflicts between sources: Discover Stradbroke lists 1 Mintee Street, Luke's own workbook lists 27 Mooloomba Road. Both are in the same village block. Coordinates left null until a local confirms.

businesses.name: Whale Tail Gelati & Coffee Bar

seasonality.pattern: Weather-led rather than calendar-led. A hot Sunday out of season outsells a cold Christmas week. Closes earlier through winter.

businesses.role_in_sim: Temperature-sensitive demand node; good test case for a system where weather drives trade rather than the calendar.
businesses.note: Formerly traded as Oceanic Gelati & Coffee Bar at the same site; older guides and review pages still use the old name.

businesses.name: Bella Balena Gelateria

seasonality.pattern: Second gelato outlet in the village; same weather-led pattern as Whale Tail, and the two split the same summer crowd.

businesses.role_in_sim: Competitor to Whale Tail in the same street; useful for modelling two shops sharing one demand pool.
businesses.note: Appears in one current listing only. Confirm it is still trading before a player sees it.

businesses.name: Loaves Bakery

seasonality.pattern: Early trade, sells out rather than extends hours. Peak season means an earlier sell-out, not a later close.

businesses.role_in_sim: The Point Lookout bakery; models a supply-limited business that sells out early rather than scaling.
businesses.note: One current listing only. The brief called this 'the Straddie Bakery / bakery at Point Lookout'; Loaves is the name that appears in the 2026 listing.

businesses.name: Six Beaches Fish Grill & Bar
businesses.address: Shop 1, 29 Mooloomba Road, Point Lookout QLD 4183

seasonality.pattern: A sit-down dinner restaurant, so it lives on holiday weeks and weekends and trims days midweek in winter.

businesses.role_in_sim: Evening dining option in the village; competes with the pub and the surf club for the same dinner crowd.
businesses.note: Days closed are an estimate. Do not present the weekly pattern as published.

businesses.name: Oasis on Straddie

seasonality.pattern: Mexican and wood-fired pizza, and an events venue as well as a restaurant, so its calendar has spikes that are not tied to holidays.

businesses.role_in_sim: Dinner and function venue on the Dickson Way side; hosts one-off events that pull crowds outside the normal season pattern.
businesses.note: Listed as 'Oasis Mexican Cantina, East Coast Road' by one source and 'Oasis on Straddie, 83 Dickson Way' by another. Treat the street as unconfirmed.

businesses.name: Fins n Fries

seasonality.pattern: Fish and chips at the shopping village; the cheap family dinner when the pub is booked out. Long weekends double the wait, not the menu.

businesses.role_in_sim: Cheap takeaway dinner option; absorbs overflow when sit-down venues are full.
businesses.note: Coordinates are for the Meegera Place shopping village, not the individual shopfront.

businesses.name: Prawn Shack

seasonality.pattern: Local seafood retail; supply-led. A bad week at sea closes the door regardless of how many visitors are on the island.

businesses.role_in_sim: Fresh seafood retail whose opening depends on catch and weather rather than on demand.
businesses.note: Single listing. Hours largely unverified.

businesses.name: Mal Starkey Seafood and Charters

seasonality.pattern: Two businesses in one: retail seafood and offshore charters. Charters are cancelled by swell and wind, so income is weather-gated even in peak season.

businesses.role_in_sim: Local fishing economy node; a clean example of a business whose output is set by sea state, not by visitor count.

businesses.name: Point Lookout Roadhouse

seasonality.pattern: One of only three fuel points on the island and the one closest to the east coast beaches. Runs low on unleaded before a long weekend ends because restock arrives by barge.

businesses.role_in_sim: Fuel supply at the Point Lookout end; a hard constraint on 4WD beach traffic and a barge-dependent stock node.
businesses.note: Public guidance is that each township has a fuel outlet and they generally close around 6pm, and that no LPG is available on the island.

businesses.name: Straddie Eats
businesses.address: Allure Stradbroke Resort, Point Lookout QLD 4183

seasonality.pattern: Sits inside a resort, so its trade tracks that resort's occupancy more closely than the island's overall visitor number.

businesses.role_in_sim: Resort-attached breakfast and lunch outlet; demonstrates a business coupled to one accommodation provider.

businesses.name: The Point Bar and Bistro
businesses.coords_source: luke-repo-workbook, Point Lookout SLSC official contact map

seasonality.pattern: The surf club's public face. Busiest when the beach is patrolled and when a carnival or nippers session has just finished; quiet on unpatrolled winter weekdays.

businesses.role_in_sim: Food and bar arm of the surf life saving club; links volunteer patrol activity to club revenue.

businesses.name: Point Lookout Bowls Club

seasonality.pattern: Steadier than the visitor venues because members carry it through winter. Sunday markets in its grounds pull a crowd that is not there for the bowls.

businesses.role_in_sim: Members' club that doubles as market site and meeting venue; a resident-facing social node rather than a visitor one.
businesses.note: Hosts Point Lookout Markets and provides the meeting room and PA the Point Lookout Fishing Club uses.

businesses.name: Coffee in Cylinders
businesses.address: Cylinder Beach car park, Point Lookout QLD 4183

seasonality.pattern: Mobile, early and weather-dependent. Does not open in heavy rain and follows the swimming crowd to whichever beach is working.

businesses.role_in_sim: Mobile vendor that can be repositioned; a test case for agents whose location is a decision rather than a fixture.

businesses.name: Island Juice
businesses.address: Cylinder Beach car park, Point Lookout QLD 4183

seasonality.pattern: Warm-weather trade at the beach car park; likely seasonal rather than year-round.

businesses.role_in_sim: Second mobile vendor at the same car park; models vendor competition for one pitch.

businesses.name: Mint Sushi

seasonality.pattern: Small takeaway; peak season is likely the only time it runs full days.

businesses.role_in_sim: Small takeaway; marginal business that can appear and disappear between seasons.
businesses.note: Named in one agency listing with no address. Confirm before showing.

businesses.name: FoodWorks Point Lookout

seasonality.pattern: Restocked by barge, so a cancelled ferry shows up on the shelves within a day. Holiday weekends strip fresh milk, bread and ice first.

businesses.role_in_sim: Point Lookout's grocery; the clearest place to model island supply chain lag against visitor surge.
businesses.note: Locals call it Bob's Shop. The public toilet block beside it is signposted the same way.

businesses.name: Straddie Brewing Co.

seasonality.pattern: Close to the ferry terminal, so it catches the last-hour crowd waiting for a barge as well as the local Friday trade. Live music nights lift midweek numbers out of season.

businesses.role_in_sim: Dunwich-side venue with live music and food trucks; catches ferry-wait crowd and shifts night activity away from Point Lookout.

businesses.name: St Stradbroke
also_known_as: St Stradbroke Wine Bar and Cellar Door

seasonality.pattern: Morning bagels and coffee, evening wine. Two different crowds through one door, which flattens its seasonal curve compared with a pure visitor venue.

businesses.role_in_sim: Dual-mode venue (cafe by day, wine bar by night); shows a small business changing role across the day.
businesses.note: Listed as 'Brews, Bagels & Bottles'. Luke's own noticeboard data calls it a wine bar and cellar door; both descriptions point to the same business.

businesses.name: Little Ship Club
businesses.coords_source: approximate, Yabby Street / One Mile jetty area

seasonality.pattern: Waterfront bistro facing the bay, so it trades on sunsets and boating weather. Many published seasonal hours finish before full night-time.

businesses.role_in_sim: Bayside club near the One Mile jetty; ties evening activity to the boating and water-taxi side of the island rather than the surf side.
businesses.note: Club has operated since 1951. Coordinates are approximate to Yabby Street.

businesses.name: Straddie Sharks All Sports Club
also_known_as: Straddie Sharks Allsports Rugby League Club
businesses.address: 2 Ballow Road, Dunwich QLD 4183 (Ron Stark Oval)

seasonality.pattern: Football season and the Easter carnival set its year, not the tourist calendar. The clubhouse, gym and squash courts keep residents coming in the off season.

businesses.role_in_sim: Resident social hub in Dunwich with a licensed clubhouse, gym and squash courts; hosts the Easter carnival on Ron Stark Oval.
businesses.note: The club kitchen has traded as Jade Lime (Thai and Cambodian). Treat the kitchen brand as changeable and the club as the stable entity.

businesses.name: CJ's Island Pizza

seasonality.pattern: Evening-only takeaway; peak weeks mean longer waits rather than longer hours.

businesses.role_in_sim: Dunwich evening takeaway; gives the arrival township a dinner option other than the clubs.

businesses.name: Bistro Seymour
businesses.address: North Stradbroke Island Golf Club, Alfred Martin Way, Dunwich QLD 4183

seasonality.pattern: Bookings essential and limited service days, so it is capacity-capped rather than demand-capped. Golf competition days set the busy times.

businesses.role_in_sim: Restaurant inside the golf club; a booking-only venue that shows how limited capacity redistributes demand.
businesses.note: Named in one current listing. The golf club itself is well established; the restaurant brand may change.

businesses.name: Barn Cafe

seasonality.pattern: Near the school on Bingle Road, so the school-run morning is part of its trade. Less exposed to the visitor cycle than Point Lookout cafes.

businesses.role_in_sim: Resident-facing cafe near the school; a business whose weekday peak is the school run, not the ferry.

businesses.name: Dunwich Bakery

seasonality.pattern: First thing off the morning barge is a pie queue. Sells out early on holiday mornings and closes rather than restocks.

businesses.role_in_sim: Arrival-side bakery; first food stop for foot passengers off the ferry.

businesses.name: Perry's Seafood Van
businesses.address: Beside FoodWorks, Stradbroke Place, Dunwich QLD 4183

seasonality.pattern: Van trade beside the supermarket; opening days flex with season and with how the operator is going.

businesses.role_in_sim: Mobile food unit in Dunwich; low-overhead business that can open and close with demand.

businesses.name: Stradbroke Island FoodWorks

seasonality.pattern: The main supermarket for residents. Stock arrives by vehicle barge, so a weather cancellation is felt here before anywhere else.

businesses.role_in_sim: Primary island grocery; the node where ferry disruption becomes an empty shelf and a resident problem.

businesses.name: Stradbroke Island Butchery

seasonality.pattern: Order deadlines matter more than opening hours: BBQ packs for a long weekend have to be ordered before the barge.

businesses.role_in_sim: Specialist food retail with a pre-order model; introduces lead time as a mechanic.

businesses.name: Cellarbrations Dunwich

seasonality.pattern: Long weekends and New Year are its whole year in four bursts. Stock has to be barged in ahead of the crowd.

businesses.role_in_sim: Takeaway liquor; a stock-ahead business and a lever for responsible-service and late-night policy scenarios.
businesses.note: Brand affiliation could have changed. Confirm the current banner before displaying the name.

businesses.name: Spar Express Dunwich

seasonality.pattern: Convenience trade near the ferry road; catches the top-up shop rather than the weekly shop.

businesses.role_in_sim: Second grocery point in Dunwich; smaller basket, longer hours.
businesses.note: Comes from Luke's own research layer, not from a current public listing. The banner may have changed. Verify before showing.

businesses.name: The Amity Pavilion

seasonality.pattern: Amity's only pub-style venue. Fills with fishing families and campers rather than surf visitors, and the after-dark transport question is harder here because it is further from the ferry.

businesses.role_in_sim: The western township's only licensed venue; drives the late-return transport problem on the Amity side.
businesses.note: Same site previously traded as Sealevel 21. ABN Lookup shows business names Amity Pavilion and Amity Tavern North Stradbroke Island current from 23 July 2025 under TOOMEY FALCONER PTY LTD. Kitchen hours 12pm to 8pm.

businesses.name: Bo Beans Coffee

seasonality.pattern: Morning coffee for Amity locals and campers. A small, early business whose trade is set by who is camped nearby.

businesses.role_in_sim: Amity's morning coffee point; small operator whose location has moved, useful for modelling a business that relocates rather than closes.
businesses.source: https://www.bobeanscoffee.com.au/ plus user correction recorded in repo: C:/Users/sbt41/githublocal/stradbroke-grants-lab/data/entities.json
businesses.note: Location is the open question, not the business. Luke's own correction (6 May 2026) says Bo's Beans moved in with the Amity Pavilion. Public listings variously give 21 Ballow Street and 44 Sovereign Road. Address and coordinates left null.

businesses.name: Amity Point General Dealers

seasonality.pattern: Groceries, fuel, bait, tackle, hot food and camping supplies in one shop, so it is the whole retail economy of Amity Point. Bait demand spikes before dawn, not at lunchtime.

businesses.role_in_sim: Single point of supply for the western township; if it closes, Amity residents must drive to Dunwich.
businesses.note: Address conflicts: 9 Ballow Street (Yellow Pages, Luke's workbook) versus 1 Llewellyn Street (Discover Stradbroke). Directory hours commonly show 6:30am to 6:00pm seven days but this is unconfirmed.

businesses.name: Amity Point Community Club

seasonality.pattern: Family club with playground, mini golf, pool table, TAB and gaming. Theme nights (parmi Wednesday, pizza Thursday, Sunday roast) carry the quiet weeks; holidays fill the bistro.

businesses.role_in_sim: Amity's social centre and wet-weather family option; the club that keeps the western township from emptying out of season.
businesses.note: Published hours are for the bistro. Bar hours may differ.

businesses.name: Straddie Servo & Hardware

seasonality.pattern: Fuel, gas swap, firewood and ice all peak on the same Friday afternoon before a long weekend. Storm season drives the hardware side.

businesses.role_in_sim: The island's hardware and gas supply as well as fuel; the shop a resident needs before a storm and a visitor needs before a campfire.
businesses.note: Sells fuel, oil, hardware, garden, car care, plumbing, electrical, cold drinks, Swap N Go gas, firewood and ice. No LPG automotive fill on the island.

businesses.name: Australia Post Dunwich LPO

seasonality.pattern: Weekday only. Parcel volume rises with online ordering rather than with visitors, and a missed barge delays the whole day's mail.

businesses.role_in_sim: Mail and Bank@Post services; a weekday-only service that shapes resident errand routes.
businesses.source: repo: C:/Users/sbt41/githublocal/straddie-noticeboard-network/data.js (Opening Hours AU and Localmint listings, phone (07) 3409 9010)
businesses.note: Directory hours conflict between 9am-4pm and 9am-5pm. Hours are an estimate.

businesses.name: Australia Post Point Lookout LPO
businesses.address: Centrepoint Shopping Village, Shop 3, 2 Meegera Place, Point Lookout QLD 4183

seasonality.pattern: Weekday only. Visitors turn up expecting weekend service and find it shut, which is a recurring small friction in peak weeks.

businesses.role_in_sim: Point Lookout postal service; models a public expectation mismatch during holidays.
businesses.source: repo: C:/Users/sbt41/githublocal/straddie-noticeboard-network/data.js (Chamber of Commerce and Opening Hours AU listings, phone (07) 3409 8210)

businesses.name: Australia Post Amity Point LPO

seasonality.pattern: Smallest of the three postal points and the most likely to reduce hours.

businesses.role_in_sim: Amity postal point; the smallest public service node on the island.
businesses.note: Listed in Luke's workbook and an AusPost locate URL, but current service availability was not confirmed.

businesses.name: Stradbroke Pharmacy

seasonality.pattern: Script collection is a resident rhythm; visitor demand is sunscreen, bite cream and forgotten medication, and it spikes on the first hot weekend.

businesses.role_in_sim: Health retail in the arrival township; part of the chain that decides whether a resident must travel to the mainland.

businesses.name: Point Lookout Pharmacy
businesses.address: Shop 1, 4 Kennedy Drive, Point Lookout QLD 4183

seasonality.pattern: Second pharmacy, on the visitor side. Sunburn, stings and holiday illness make its peak sharper and later in the day than Dunwich's.

businesses.role_in_sim: Health retail beside the medical centre at Point Lookout; the visitor-facing half of island health services.

businesses.name: Stradbroke Island Medical Centre

seasonality.pattern: Closed weekends and public holidays, which is exactly when the island's population is largest. That gap pushes weekend presentations to the Marie Rose Centre and to the mainland.

businesses.role_in_sim: The island's general practice; its weekday-only hours are a real, modellable gap in weekend health cover.
businesses.note: Telehealth and telephone consultations offered at the same cost as face to face.

businesses.name: Marie Rose Centre
businesses.address: Corner Oxley Parade and Petrie Street, Dunwich QLD 4183

seasonality.pattern: Small rural emergency outpost of Redland Hospital, staffed for emergencies only and closed outside its hours. Anything serious after 4pm becomes a transfer problem across water.

businesses.role_in_sim: The only emergency health point on the island; its closing time is the trigger for mainland transfer scenarios.
businesses.note: Emergencies only. Non-emergency cases are directed to a GP or 13 HEALTH.

businesses.name: Yulu-Burri-Ba Aboriginal Corporation for Community Health

seasonality.pattern: Serves the resident Aboriginal community year round, so its load does not follow the tourist curve at all. It is the counter-example to every visitor-driven business in this file.

businesses.role_in_sim: Community-controlled primary health, dental and social health services; a resident-load service that stays flat while visitor services spike.
businesses.note: Also operates clinics off the island (Capalaba, Wynnum). Appointments required; no payment or Medicare card needed. Headcount estimate covers the island clinic only and is uncertain.

businesses.name: Straddie Super Sports

seasonality.pattern: Opens early for fishers and campers arriving on the first barge. Bait, ice and tackle sell before dawn; camping gear sells on arrival day.

businesses.role_in_sim: The only outdoor and sporting goods shop on the island; the gear bottleneck for fishing, camping and beach agents.
businesses.note: The brief mentioned bike and 4WD hire here; that was not confirmed. Treat it as an outdoor gear and sporting goods shop until a local says otherwise.

businesses.name: Noreen's Seaside Shop
businesses.address: Shop 1, Anchorage on Straddie, 112 Dickson Way, Point Lookout QLD 4183

seasonality.pattern: Gift retail lives entirely on visitors. Empty weeks in winter, full days in January.

businesses.role_in_sim: Discretionary retail; the first kind of business to feel a drop in visitor numbers.

businesses.name: Linen Caravan

seasonality.pattern: Homewares and linen, so it also supplies the holiday letting stock, which gives it a second, less visible customer.

businesses.role_in_sim: Retail with a business-to-business side supplying holiday houses; a small hidden link in the letting economy.

businesses.name: Starfish Studio

seasonality.pattern: Artist-run retail; opening hours flex with the maker's own work and with the arts trail calendar.

businesses.role_in_sim: Maker-run shopfront; models a business where the owner's other work sets the opening hours.

businesses.name: Salt Water Murris

seasonality.pattern: Gallery trade follows the ferry and the festival calendar. Exhibition openings, not holidays, are its biggest days.

businesses.role_in_sim: Quandamooka art gallery near the ferry; a cultural retail node whose calendar runs on exhibitions.
businesses.note: Cultural entity. Any depiction in the world must follow the cultural care rules in docs/CULTURAL-REVIEW.md; do not attach invented cultural content to it.

businesses.name: Delvene Cockatoo-Collins studio and shopfront

seasonality.pattern: Artist-led opening. Studio hours depend on commissions and exhibitions rather than on visitor numbers.

businesses.role_in_sim: Quandamooka artist shopfront in Dunwich; part of the creative economy layer.
businesses.note: A named living person's business. Do not put words, story or cultural content in her mouth in the simulation.

businesses.name: Straddie Kingfisher Tours

seasonality.pattern: Half and full day 4WD eco tours. Whale watching from June to November is the drawcard; tours are cancelled or rerouted by beach conditions and tide.

businesses.role_in_sim: 4WD tour operator; puts vehicles on the beach and links tourism income to tide and dune condition.
businesses.note: Operating over 25 years; the family has been on the island since 1966.

businesses.name: Straddie Adventures

seasonality.pattern: Bay kayaking and sandboarding, both weather dependent. Bookings need to be phoned ahead, so its capacity is set by the operator's own availability, not by demand.

businesses.role_in_sim: Quandamooka-owned adventure and cultural tour operator based at One Mile; an owner-operator whose availability is the constraint.
businesses.note: Owned and operated by Traditional Owners of Quandamooka. Operating since 1998. Cultural content belongs to them; do not script it.

businesses.name: North Stradbroke Island Surf School

seasonality.pattern: Lessons run on small, clean surf. A big swell that thrills surfers cancels the school, so its good days are not the beach's most dramatic ones.

businesses.role_in_sim: Surf lessons; a business that wants moderate swell, which puts it in tension with the surf conditions the island is famous for.

businesses.name: Yura Tours

seasonality.pattern: Cultural tours run to a booking calendar rather than a shopfront roster; school and group bookings sit outside the holiday peak.

businesses.role_in_sim: Cultural tour operator; brings group and school bookings that do not follow the holiday curve.
businesses.note: Cultural operator. No cultural content should be generated for it in the simulation.

businesses.name: Goompi Trail

seasonality.pattern: Guided heritage walk in Dunwich; runs to booking demand and to guide availability.

businesses.role_in_sim: Guided heritage walk on the Dunwich foreshore; a walking activity that does not need a vehicle.
businesses.note: Confirmed as a listed heritage walk; the operating entity and schedule were not confirmed. Cultural content is not ours to write.

businesses.name: SeaLink South East Queensland
businesses.address: Middle Street terminal, Cleveland QLD 4163 to Junner Street, Dunwich QLD 4183

seasonality.pattern: The whole island's throttle. Extra services run for holidays; the vehicle queue at Cleveland on a Friday before a long weekend is the island's defining crowd scene. Cancellations for weather cascade into grocery stock, staff shifts and medical transfers.

businesses.role_in_sim: Primary vehicle and passenger link. Capacity here sets the ceiling on every other system in the world.
businesses.note: Fleet capacities recorded in Luke's research notes: Minjerribah 52 cars / 400 passengers, Sea Breeze 60 cars / 300 passengers, Quandamooka 52 cars / 400 passengers, Yalingbila 198 passengers. Crossing listed at 45 to 50 minutes. Hours are an estimate; use the published timetable for real service times.

businesses.name: Stradbroke Flyer Gold Cats
businesses.address: Cleveland to One Mile jetty, Dunwich QLD 4183

seasonality.pattern: Foot passengers only, roughly 25 minutes, with a free mainland bus and no online bookings. That walk-up behaviour means its queue forms differently from the vehicle ferry's: later, and with no reservation to fall back on.

businesses.role_in_sim: Passenger-only water taxi to a different arrival point (One Mile), splitting arrivals across two terminals and two townships.
businesses.note: Arrives at One Mile, not at the Dunwich vehicle terminal. This distinction matters for wayfinding and bus connections.

businesses.name: Stradbroke Island Buses

seasonality.pattern: Timetable is written to meet the barge, so a late ferry ripples straight into missed connections. Seasonal timetables add capacity for school holidays, public holidays and weekends.

businesses.role_in_sim: Route 880 (Dunwich to Point Lookout) and 881 (Dunwich to Amity Point) carry every arriving foot passenger; the connection failure mode is the whole game.
businesses.note: Acquired by Transit Systems; services run under Translink. The 1 December 2025 Translink update extended route 881 to Dunwich, added a QUAMPI stop and added 880 services. Charter vehicles listed at 40 to 62 seats.

businesses.name: Stradbroke Cab Service

seasonality.pattern: Two vans for the whole island, so late-night demand after a pub or club night exceeds supply on any busy Saturday.

businesses.role_in_sim: Late-night and accessible transport; a hard-capped resource that fails visibly on busy nights.
businesses.note: Public listing describes two 10-seat commuter vans, one wheelchair accessible. Confirm the service is still running before relying on it.

businesses.name: StradEasy

seasonality.pattern: Pre-booked ferry-to-door transfers from both Dunwich and One Mile. Group bookings cluster around arrival waves rather than spreading through the day.

businesses.role_in_sim: Booked private transfer with up to 11 seats; the paid alternative when the bus is full or the last one has gone.

businesses.name: Quandamooka Yoolooburrabee Aboriginal Corporation (QYAC)

seasonality.pattern: Not a seasonal business. It is the Native Title body and land manager, and it owns the camping operation, so holiday pressure reaches it as a land management and cultural care load rather than as trade.

businesses.role_in_sim: Registered Native Title body corporate for Quandamooka Country; land and sea management, ranger program, camping operation and cultural authority. Nothing cultural enters the world without a citable source and a human review.
businesses.note: Cultural authority. See docs/CULTURAL-REVIEW.md. Headcount is an estimate across the corporation, rangers and camping business, and is uncertain.

businesses.name: QUAMPI, the Quandamooka Arts and Culture Centre

seasonality.pattern: Exhibition-led rather than holiday-led. Opening weekends and the Quandamooka Festival drive its biggest days, and the new bus stop feeds it foot traffic year round.

businesses.role_in_sim: Exhibition, event and performance venue with cafe and gift shop; a new civic anchor in Dunwich that changes where visitors stop after the ferry.
businesses.note: Opened 11 September 2025. Indigenous owned and operated. Route 881 was extended to include a QUAMPI stop from 1 December 2025.

businesses.name: Minjerribah Moorgumpin Elders-in-Council Aboriginal Corporation (MMEIC)

seasonality.pattern: Not seasonal. Cultural governance and Elders' guidance run to community need.

businesses.role_in_sim: Elders' council providing cultural guidance; present in the world as a civic body, never as a source of scripted cultural content.
businesses.note: Confirmed in Luke's own research layer. A current public address and hours were not confirmed.

businesses.name: Dunwich State School

seasonality.pattern: The inverse of every other entry: school holidays empty it while they fill the island. School terms are what make Dunwich a working town on a Tuesday morning.

businesses.role_in_sim: The only school on Minjerribah, Prep to Year 6, drawing from all three townships; sets the weekday morning traffic and the bus pattern.
businesses.note: Opened 1904. Secondary students travel to the mainland, which is a real daily ferry dependency for island families.

businesses.name: Point Lookout Surf Life Saving Club

seasonality.pattern: Patrols run to the surf life saving season and to volunteer availability, not to visitor numbers. The mismatch is the point: the busiest unpatrolled days are the dangerous ones.

businesses.role_in_sim: Volunteer beach patrol at Main Beach; the gap between patrol hours and swimmer numbers is a first-class safety mechanic.
businesses.note: Patrol hours listed here are an estimate. Use Surf Life Saving Queensland's published patrol calendar for real ones.

businesses.name: Point Lookout Fishing Club
businesses.coords_source: luke-repo-workbook, Point Lookout Bowls Club site

seasonality.pattern: Competition dates and weigh-ins set the calendar. Junior clinics run in holidays; the club's real season is the fish, not the tourists.

businesses.role_in_sim: Volunteer fishing club meeting at the Bowls Club; a source of catch data, junior programs and the kind of local knowledge no dashboard has.
businesses.note: Meets at the Point Lookout Bowls Club and uses its room and PA. Meeting night shown here is an estimate.

businesses.name: North Stradbroke Island Golf Club

seasonality.pattern: Members carry it midweek; competition days and visitor rounds lift the weekend. Inland site, so it is less affected by wind than the coastal venues.

businesses.role_in_sim: Inland recreation and function venue; a resident activity that continues when the coast is unusable.
businesses.note: Par 71, roughly 5282 yards.

businesses.name: North Stradbroke Island Museum on Minjerribah

seasonality.pattern: Volunteer-staffed, so its opening days depend on who is available. Wet holiday days are its busiest.

businesses.role_in_sim: Local history museum near the ferry; the wet-weather destination and a legible source of island history for a player.
businesses.note: Address given variously as 15-17 and 15-18 Welsby Street.

businesses.name: Straddie Chamber of Commerce

seasonality.pattern: Volunteer-led, so it works between seasons rather than during them. Advocacy activity rises when ferry capacity, parking or planning decisions are in front of council.

businesses.role_in_sim: The organised voice of island business in consultation scenarios; a bloc a civic planner has to answer to.
businesses.note: Formed after the 2011 suspension of sand mining to support the transition to a visitor economy. Volunteer-led not-for-profit.

businesses.name: North Stradbroke Island Rural Fire Brigade

seasonality.pattern: Fire season on a sand island is its own calendar: dry spring winds and holiday campfires, not summer heat alone. Volunteer availability drops exactly when visitor numbers peak.

businesses.role_in_sim: Volunteer fire response across all three townships; the crew that has to be found before a fire can be fought.
businesses.note: There is also a Queensland Fire Department station at Dunwich. Brigade structure and station addresses were not confirmed in detail.

businesses.name: Queensland Ambulance Service, Dunwich station

seasonality.pattern: Case load rises with visitor numbers and with surf. Serious cases need a transfer across water, so response time is not the whole story here.

businesses.role_in_sim: Ambulance cover in the arrival township; the start of every off-island medical transfer chain.
businesses.note: Address from a secondary source. Confirm before using it as a map pin.

businesses.name: Queensland Ambulance Service, Point Lookout

seasonality.pattern: Closest response to the surf beaches, so its load tracks beach conditions and patrol gaps.

businesses.role_in_sim: Second ambulance point, closer to the beaches; halves response distance to the east coast.
businesses.note: Address from a secondary source and staffing model not confirmed.

businesses.name: Queensland Police Service, Dunwich station

seasonality.pattern: Extra officers are brought over for big holiday weekends, which is a visible sign in itself that the island's population has changed shape.

businesses.role_in_sim: Island police presence; reinforcement from the mainland during peak weekends is a modellable civic decision.
businesses.note: Station confirmed by reference to Dunwich police; street address and hours not confirmed.

businesses.name: Volunteer Marine Rescue North Stradbroke

seasonality.pattern: Callouts follow boating traffic and weather change, so the worst days are the ones where a fine morning turns bad by lunchtime.

businesses.role_in_sim: Volunteer marine rescue for Moreton Bay waters; the response layer for the boating half of island life.
businesses.note: Confirmed in Luke's research layer. Base address and radio schedule not confirmed.

businesses.name: North Stradbroke Island Recycling and Waste Centre
businesses.address: Dickson Way, North Stradbroke Island QLD 4183

seasonality.pattern: Waste volume follows visitors with a one-day lag: campgrounds and holiday houses empty out on Sunday afternoon and Monday morning. Everything has to leave the island by barge.

businesses.role_in_sim: Waste and recycling transfer point; closes the loop on the visitor system and shows the barge working in the other direction.
businesses.note: Sources give two locations, Dickson Way and East Coast Road. They may be one facility described two ways. Free for residents, fees for commercial users and non-residents.

businesses.name: Redland City Council

seasonality.pattern: Not seasonal in staffing, but its island workload is: parks, waste, roads, venue bookings and camping pressure all peak in the same weeks.

businesses.role_in_sim: Local government: parks, halls, waste, roads, venue booking and planning approvals. The counterparty in every civic planning scenario.
businesses.note: Council is headquartered at Cleveland. Whether there is a staffed island customer counter was not confirmed; island-based staff numbers are a guess.

businesses.name: Dunwich Public Hall

seasonality.pattern: Booked rather than open. Its role rises in bad weather and in emergencies, when an indoor space with a kitchen becomes the most useful building in town.

businesses.role_in_sim: Indoor community venue and wet-weather fallback; also the natural evacuation or briefing space in a disaster scenario.
businesses.note: St Mark's Anglican Church and Dunwich Public Hall are heritage listed. Hall management arrangements were not confirmed.

businesses.name: Point Lookout Community Hall

seasonality.pattern: Booked venue for concerts, talks, workshops and markets; it fills the gap when an outdoor event is rained out.

businesses.role_in_sim: Point Lookout's indoor gathering space; the wet-weather alternative for beach events.

businesses.name: Amity Point Public Hall

seasonality.pattern: Small hall, booked for meetings and community events; the only indoor public room in the western township.

businesses.role_in_sim: Amity Point's public room; the meeting place when a decision affects the western township.
businesses.note: Recorded on a Redland City Council local heritage card.

businesses.name: Nareeba Moopi Moopi Pa aged care hostel

seasonality.pattern: Constant load. Staffing is the constraint, and staff housing on the island is the constraint on staffing.

businesses.role_in_sim: Aged care on the island; lets Elders and older residents stay on Country instead of moving to the mainland.
businesses.note: From Luke's own research layer. Current operating status, operator and address were not confirmed. Verify before showing.

businesses.name: North Stradbroke Island Aboriginal and Islander Housing Society

seasonality.pattern: Not seasonal, but under permanent pressure from holiday letting: every house converted to short stay is a house not available to a resident family.

businesses.role_in_sim: Community housing provider; the counterweight to holiday letting in any housing scenario.
businesses.note: From Luke's own research layer. Current operating status and address not confirmed.

businesses.name: Wildlife Rescue Minjerribah

seasonality.pattern: Callouts rise with traffic: more cars on the island means more koala, kangaroo and bird strikes, and holiday weekends are the worst of it.

businesses.role_in_sim: Volunteer wildlife rescue; connects the ecology systems to the traffic and visitor systems through a human response chain.
businesses.note: Luke has built a wildlife rescue app for this workflow. Wildcare Straddie appears alongside it in his data as a related fauna care network.

businesses.name: Friends of Stradbroke Island

seasonality.pattern: Campaign-driven rather than seasonal. Activity spikes around planning decisions, water and aquifer questions and development applications.

businesses.role_in_sim: Environmental advocacy group; an organised objector or supporter in civic consultation scenarios.
businesses.note: Long-standing group with a public record in Queensland Parliament submissions. Current activity level not confirmed.

businesses.name: Point Lookout Bushcare

seasonality.pattern: Working bees run in cooler months and after rain, when weeds pull easily. Volunteer numbers fall in summer, which is when weeds grow fastest.

businesses.role_in_sim: Weed control working bees; a slow, cumulative ecological effect driven by volunteer hours rather than money.
businesses.note: Working bee days shown are an estimate.

businesses.name: Point Lookout Markets
businesses.address: Point Lookout Bowls Club, 75 Dickson Way, Point Lookout QLD 4183

seasonality.pattern: Runs to a Sunday and holiday pattern at the Bowls Club. Stallholder numbers rise in holiday periods; a wet Sunday cancels it outright.

businesses.role_in_sim: Recurring market that turns a club car park into a crowd node one morning a week; a clean test of temporary land use.
businesses.note: Historically tied to Sunday and holiday patterns. Exact current frequency not confirmed.

businesses.name: Straddie Mobile Vet

seasonality.pattern: Mobile and appointment-based. After hours and emergency work goes to mainland hospitals, which means a ferry trip with a sick animal.

businesses.role_in_sim: The island's veterinary cover; another service where the fallback is a ferry crossing.
businesses.note: Listed on the island services page as a mobile service. Emergency and after hours work is referred to mainland hospitals at Manly West, Thornlands and Cleveland.

businesses.name: Sandy Sports Club

seasonality.pattern: Not applicable. This entity does not trade.

businesses.role_in_sim: Proposed incorporated association for beach sport, youth programs, cultural activation and outdoor cinema. Include only as a clearly labelled proposal, never as an operating club.
businesses.note: This is Luke's own proposed entity, not an existing club. It is in this file because the contract allows proposed things if they are marked as proposed. Do not render it as a real venue.

businesses.name: Rufus King Seafoods

seasonality.pattern: Not applicable. Closed.

businesses.role_in_sim: Historical only. Kept in the file so a future agent does not re-add it from a stale web listing.
